evidence.evidence_quote: It is good practice to use the with keyword when dealing with file objects.  The advantage is that the file is properly closed after its suite finishes, even if an exception is raised at some point.  Using !with is also much shorter than writing equivalent try\ -\ finally blocks::

with open("myfile.txt") as f:
       for line in f:
           print(line, end="")

After the statement is executed, the file *f* is always closed, even if a problem was encountered while processing the lines. Objects which, like files, provide predefined clean-up actions will indicate this in their documentation.
